To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have cloned, characterized, and expressed a novel iridoid synthases from Antirrhinus majus (AmIYS) which catalyses the conversion of 8-geranylgeranyl-PP to 7-epiloganin, and that the stereocontrol of the reaction differs from that of the Catharanthos homologue CrIYS.

(i) AmISY is an enzyme that is responsible, in a two-step reaction, for the formation of a bicyclic iridoindole scaffold in snapdragon; (ii) the enzyme catalyzes the opposite stereochemical reduction step compared to its homologue in Catharanthus rosea; (iii) in contrast, both AmISY, and its homologue CrIS in C. rosea, catalyze the cyclization step with a low degree of stereose
the iridoid cyclases from snapdragon and Catharanthus roseu s are stereospecific, but the cyclization reaction is not completely stereoselective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the biosynthetic origin of the iridoids in A. majus and the elucidation of their biosynthetic pathways.
the discovery, cloning and characterization of iridoid synthesis genes in plants.

the elucidation of the biosynthesis of the iridoid scaffold, which is the basis of the chemical diversity of this natural product class, and with the identification of the enzymes involved in iridoid biosynthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stereoselective reduction step of iridoid synthesis is controlled by the iridoid biosynthesis pathway and that the cyclization is controlled by the enzyme itself.
AmISY and its homologue from the closely related species Plantago lanceolata catalyze the same reaction with the same stereoselectivity, but with opposite stereocontrol at C7.
AmISY and the Catharanthus enzyme are stereospecific, but not stereoselective, in their cyclization step.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iridoids are synthesized by two enzymes that are structurally similar but catalyze the same reactions in opposite stereochemical configurations.
iridoid synthases catalyze a reduction–cyclization cascade, but the stereocontrol of the cyclization step is not as strong as that of the reduction.
AmISY is a stereospecific enzyme, whereas CrISY is a diastereoselective enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stereochemistry of the cyclization step in iridoid synthases can be altered by subtle changes in the amino-acid sequence.
iridoid synthases are not rigidly constrained to produce the same stereochemistry.
AmISY and the other plant iridoid synthases are highly stereoselective enzymes, which can produce the bicyclic core of iridoid natural products with high enantiomeric purity.
